sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Duval County?
sections.html:
Two offices do most of the work: the Duval County Property Appraiser sets values and decides exemptions, and the Duval County Tax Collector bills and collects. Duval County and the City of Jacksonville are served through the same Jacksonville.gov web presence, so both offices sit on the city's site.

The Property Appraiser's customer service and exemptions division is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone 904-255-5900. The Tax Collector's main address is 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone (904) 255-5700, with weekday counter hours that start at 8:30 a.m. For value appeals, the Value Adjustment Board answers at (904) 255-5124.

  • Questions about ownership, exemptions or an assessed value: Property Appraiser.
  • Questions about a bill, a payment or a delinquent account: Tax Collector, taxcollector@coj.net.
  • Questions about a petition against your value: Value Adjustment Board.

If you plan to sell, you will deal with all three at different points, and the clerk of the court records the deed.

sections.h2: Which taxing districts apply to a house in Duval County?
sections.html:
The district code on your parcel decides which millage applies, and Duval County has six of them. The Property Appraiser lists them as GS and USD1 for the City of Jacksonville, USD2 for Jacksonville Beach, USD3 for Atlantic Beach, USD4 for Neptune Beach and USD5 for Baldwin.

Each district's total millage is built from several authorities. For the county the listed authorities are the county, the public schools, the Florida Inland Navigation District and the St. Johns River Water Management District, with the beach cities and Baldwin adding their own levies where they apply. The Property Appraiser states that homeowners and business owners pay the same millage inside one district unless a statute or local ordinance exempts them.

Two houses with the same value can therefore have different bills if one is in Jacksonville Beach and the other is in Jacksonville proper. The Property Appraiser posts millage charts by year, including 2025, on its Millage Rates page.

sections.h2: What are the key property tax dates for Duval County owners?
sections.html:
The year runs on a fixed Florida calendar, and the table below pairs each step with what the Duval offices print.

Property tax calendar as printed by Florida DOR and the Duval County Property Appraiser
WhenWhat happensSource
January 1Value and ownership are fixed for the tax yearFlorida DOR
March 1Filing deadline for exemptions; for the 2027 roll the Property Appraiser lists March 1, 2027Property Appraiser
April 1Tangible personal property returns dueProperty Appraiser
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed; in 2026 they went out August 14Property Appraiser
SeptemberPublic hearings to set budgets and millageProperty Appraiser
October 13, 20262026 final tax roll certifiedProperty Appraiser
NovemberTax bills mailed, with a 4 percent discount for November paymentFlorida DOR
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquentFlorida DOR

Florida DOR gives the discount ladder as 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. After delinquency, tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

sections.h2: How does the Duval County homestead exemption work?
sections.html:
Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value for a permanent residence you owned and lived in on January 1. The first $25,000 applies to every levy including school taxes, and the second $25,000 applies only to value above $50,000 and only to non-school levies. Florida DOR notes the second slice is adjusted for inflation each year.

The Duval Property Appraiser accepts an online application for owners who moved in after January 1, 2026, and the deadline to file on time for the 2027 roll is March 1, 2027. Late filing is allowed until the 25th day after TRIM notices go out, which falls in early September. A paper application can be mailed to Suite 260 at 231 E. Forsyth Street, faxed to (904) 255-7963 or emailed to pacustserv@coj.net.

  • Save Our Homes holds yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. DOR's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1, so a buyer does not inherit your capped value.
  • Portability lets you carry some of the cap to a new Florida homestead if you set it up within three years.

sections.h2: How do I challenge my Duval County property value?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review at the Property Appraiser, then file a petition with the Value Adjustment Board if you still disagree. The petition deadline is printed on your TRIM notice and, under the state rule, runs 25 days from the date the notice was mailed.

A petition has a payment condition. The Property Appraiser warns that petitioners generally must pay 75 percent of the ad valorem tax, plus all non-ad valorem assessments, before the delinquency date, usually April 1, or the petition can be denied. Call the Value Adjustment Board at (904) 255-5124 to confirm the amount for your case.

If you ask for your property record card on the petition form, the Property Appraiser now supplies it online through Property Search under the TRIM record section rather than mailing it. Denials of exemptions or portability follow a separate path: the clock for those is 30 days from the mailing of the denial letter.

sections.h2: What happens to the property tax bill when I sell a Duval County house?
sections.html:
The bill follows the parcel, so unpaid tax must be cleared or settled at closing. Florida law makes the owner responsible for knowing that tax is due and paying before April 1 of the following year, and the Property Appraiser lists ownership as of January 1.

A few points matter at a Duval closing:

  • Ask the Tax Collector for the current amount owed on the parcel before you sign a contract, including any delinquent years.
  • If a mortgage servicer escrows your tax, confirm with them what has been paid and what a refund looks like after payoff.
  • Deed documentary stamp tax in Duval is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party to the deed is liable even if the contract assigns it to one side. It is collected by the clerk when the deed records.
  • Do not rely on aerial photos on the Property Appraiser's site for boundaries. The office tells buyers and sellers to use a surveyor and a title company.

The Clerk offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails you within 48 hours when a document is recorded under a name you watch, which is worth setting up if you own a vacant or inherited house.

sections.h2: Does a rental or short-term rental change Duval property tax?
sections.html:
Yes. Renting a home can end the homestead, and furnishings in a rental count as taxable personal property. Florida DOR states that homestead is lost when the unit is rented or stops being the permanent home.

The Property Appraiser explains that household goods are excluded from tangible personal property only for an owner's own use. Once the home is a short-term or long-term rental, the furniture and appliances are treated as tangible personal property, and anyone owning such property on January 1 must file a return by April 1. Short-term transient rentals also owe additional sales and use tax to the Tax Collector monthly, and hosting sites such as Airbnb and VRBO do not remit it for owners. Email TouristTax@coj.net for the rules.

sections.h2: Can an older, disabled or veteran owner pay less?
sections.html:
Several Florida relief programs exist, and each needs its own application with the Property Appraiser or Tax Collector. Ask which ones your parcel qualifies for before the March 1 filing date.

  • A disabled ex-servicemember with a rating of 10 percent or more can get a $5,000 reduction in assessed value.
  • A veteran with a permanent service-connected disability who is 65 or older may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage.
  • A total and permanent service-connected disability can qualify for a full exemption on homestead.
  • Homestead tax deferral is requested with Form DR-570 from the Tax Collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

Cities and counties may also adopt an extra exemption of up to $50,000 for owners 65 or older within an income limit. Ask the Property Appraiser whether Duval has adopted it and what the current income limit is.

faqs.q: When are Duval County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in November and are payable then, with a 4 percent discount for November payment. Unpaid tax becomes delinquent April 1, and certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1. Call (904) 255-5700 for the amount on a specific parcel.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Duval homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year. For the 2027 roll the Property Appraiser lists March 1, 2027, with late filing allowed until early September, the 25th day after TRIM notices are mailed.

faqs.q: Do I pay the same millage anywhere in Duval County?
faqs.a: No. Millage depends on your taxing district: Jacksonville (GS and USD1), Jacksonville Beach, Atlantic Beach, Neptune Beach or Baldwin. The Property Appraiser's Millage Rates page lists each year's charts.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed stamp tax when I sell in Duval County?
faqs.a: The statute makes every party to the deed liable at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, whatever the contract says. The clerk collects it at recording, so settle in writing who covers it before closing.

faqs.q: Where can I report suspected exemption fraud in Duval County?
faqs.a: Call the Property Appraiser's exemption fraud hotline at (904) 255-7964. For billing problems, contact the Tax Collector at taxcollector@coj.net or (904) 255-5700.
